entries.core_move: Interpret a continuous-time system as a rule that transforms an input signal into an output signal, connecting the system-as-transformation view to later filters, circuits, differential-equation models, and system-property tests.

Distinguish the input signal, output signal, and transformation direction for a continuous-time system so a situation can be framed as an input-output model before applying system notation and system-property tests.
Interpret continuous-time system notation such as $x(t)$ -> $y(t)$ and $y(t) = T{x(t)} by identifying the input signal$, system operator, and output signal in an input-output model.
Map a filter description into continuous-time system notation by identifying the input signal, output signal, and the signal feature the filter passes, attenuates, or modifies.

Model an RC circuit as a continuous-time input-output system by assigning a source signal as the input, choosing a circuit variable as the output, and interpreting the circuit relation as the system rule.

Represent automobile motion as a continuous-time input-output system by selecting physical input and output signals and expressing their relationship as a system rule such as integrating acceleration to obtain velocity or position.
Convert a differential equation into a continuous-time input-output model by identifying the input, output, derivative orders, and the equation rule that determines the output from the input.
